title: Master Class | Danish ACCEPTED!! | Chess Speedrun | Grandmaster Naroditsky

moves.spoken: We take White; Black meets our king's pawn with ...e5.
We build the centre with d4.
Black takes on d4.
We offer c3 — the Danish Gambit.
Black takes on c3, accepting.
We develop the bishop to c4 — the heart of the Danish.
Black plays the queen to e7 — targeting our pawn, but with nothing else developed it's a poor way to do it, and it blocks in his own bishop.
We recapture on c3 with the knight — two pieces out already, and that queen on e7 is a liability.
Black plays c6.
We develop the knight to f3. If ...d5 comes, so much the better — with our lead in development we want the centre opened.
Black plays h6 — you can't abandon development like this; it will backfire in a few moves.
We simply castle — no need for wild sacrifices; completing development already does us a huge favour.
Black plays d6, the lesser evil. Now for a little creativity — rather than the murky e5 break with a sacrifice on d5, notice the queen and king sitting on the same file.
We slide the rook to e1 — queen and king share the e-file. The e4-pawn is in the way for now, but this sets up the knight to d5.
Black develops the bishop to e6.
The knight leaps to d5 — not really a sacrifice, since ...cxd5 is met by exd5, reopening lines and prying open the e-file.
Black takes the knight, a pawn landing on d5.
We recapture on d5, and now the bishop on e6 is attacked — once it falls the whole position caves in.
Black finally develops the knight to f6 — but here developing is the decisive mistake.
We take the bishop, our pawn landing on e6.
Black tries the knight to e4.
We simply take it with the rook.
Black plays f6.
The knight swings to h4, eyeing the juicy light squares — g6 is coming.
Black develops the knight to c6.
We drop the knight into g6, heading straight for the rook.
Black plays the queen to c7; the knight crashes in and takes the rook — up a rook and a piece, it's time for Black to resign.
